title: Refactor Asset Identification to UUIDs and Implement Data Migration
description: The LedgerView Media Suite currently uses sequential integer IDs for media assets. This is fragile and can lead to data conflicts when merging projects created on different machines. The goal is to upgrade the asset identification system to use universally unique identifiers (UUIDs). This is a complex, multi-stage task that requires a core refactoring, fixing the widespread breakage caused by the change, and finally implementing a data migration path to ensure backward compatibility with older project files.

project_spec.name: LedgerView Media Suite
project_spec.description:
LedgerView Media Suite is an enterprise-grade desktop media management console built in C for finance and insurance companies that must curate, annotate, and audit rich-media assets used in client-facing pitches and regulatory reports. The application delivers a multi-window GUI where analysts can drag-and-drop videos, images, and annotated spreadsheets into presentation playlists, track version histories, and enforce corporate branding through customizable themes and keyboard-driven workflows.  

Designed around a strict hexagonal architecture, LedgerView separates its business-critical rules—such as compliance watermarks, retention policies, and audit logging—from volatile infrastructure concerns like GUI toolkits, file systems, or third-party codecs. Adapters expose uniform ports for media ingestion, reporting, and plugin extensions, allowing risk-management teams to hot-swap new encryption or crash-reporting modules without touching the domain core. The suite embeds a Plugin Architecture combined with Command, Observer, and State Machine patterns to orchestrate real-time collaboration, auto-updates, granular user preferences, and automated rollback on failed jobs, ensuring uninterrupted productivity in high-stakes business environments.
